title: Rename Middleware to Proxy without changing routing intent
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed proxy.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Compare the 15 middleware and 16 proxy path coverage.
Build without an unsupported Proxy runtime export.
Verify unrelated assets are not intercepted and protected actions still authorize internally.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: Filename, export and runtime rules migrate together.
Compare the 15 middleware and 16 proxy path coverage.
alternativeApproaches: Prefer bounded lightweight routing checks and enforce real authorization near data access. Database work in the routing layer can become a latency and availability dependency for every matched request.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Compare the 15 middleware and 16 proxy path coverage.
Build without an unsupported Proxy runtime export.
Verify unrelated assets are not intercepted and protected actions still authorize internally.
nextjsPractice.next15: Keep this logic in middleware.ts with the middleware export. Runtime support depends on the exact 15.x release; do not assume all 15 patches share Node middleware support.
nextjsPractice.next16: Use proxy.ts and proxy. Proxy defaults to Node.js; setting the runtime export in the Proxy file is unsupported.
